the study of the role of ciliary function in the pathogenesis of hydrocephalus and the role of ependymal and choroid plexuses in regulating CSF flow.

the MCIDAS-associated hydrocephalus is not progressive, but it is associated with a significant risk for the development of arachnoid and other brain abnormalities.
the presence of hydrocephalus with CPH is a strong clue that a patient may have a PCD-associated MCIDAS mutation, and that this may lead to a diagnosis of RGMC.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MCIDAS mutation causes hydrocephalus and choroid plexopathy.
we have found a new neuroradiologic feature associated with MCIDAS mutations and reduced motile cilia.

hydrocephalus and CPH are a new phenotypic association with PCD.
